source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
notes: Another piece of evidence that in (85) and similar examples we are not dealing with thematically determined accusative case comes from the contrast between causative intransitives and causative transitives with respect to passivization. As shown in (86), an unergative-based causative verb can be passivized, both lexically and syntactically. This supports the view advocated above that accusative case in (86a) is the result of a lexicon-marking procedure assigning ACC to xaamtar ‘make walk’ ([+c+m], [-c+m]). On the contrary, (87) – the passive counterpart of (85) with accusative Aisen is ungrammatical.
en: Aisen was made to boil water.
